about: Model verdicts on source against tree for pd-householder-guide (system/rag/semcheck.py).

findings.problem: The key of the curtilage diagram is read as a one-column table with an invented heading, and the diagram itself is not kept as a figure, so the tree does not say which area is white.
findings.evidence: source: diagram with key "Curtilage of house" (white box), "Original house" (blue box) / tree: table, columns "Diagram key"

findings.problem: The numbered limits A.1 (a) and (b) and their explanations are run together into one block of body text instead of separate provisions.
findings.evidence: tree: "A.1 Development is not permitted by Class A if – (a) permission to use the dwellinghouse ... (change of use) Enlargement etc. is not permitted"

findings.problem: The printed page number is kept inside the running text.
findings.evidence: source: "50% of the white area." / tree: "would be 50% of the white area. 10 (c) the height of the part"

findings.problem: The printed page number is kept inside the body text at the end of the paragraph.
findings.evidence: source: "any extension of a house is to be made." / tree: "any extension of a house is to be made. 13"

findings.problem: Labels printed inside the two drawings are run into the end of the body paragraph, with the page number.
findings.evidence: source: "will follow these walls." / tree: "will follow these walls. Highway Walls Forming Principal Elevation Highway Highway 15"

findings.problem: A drawing label is kept as a body text section of its own and again as a table row.
findings.evidence: tree: "Any extension forward of this line will not be permitted development and will require an application for planning permission"

findings.problem: The page sits under a heading "X" that is not in the document, so Class A limit (h) is not under Class A.
findings.evidence: source: "h) the enlarged part of the dwellinghouse would have more than a single storey" / tree heading_path: "X > Text"

findings.problem: A bold sub-heading and the new provision (h) are read as running body text in one block with the earlier text.
findings.evidence: tree: "9m A B 19 Side wall extensions extending beyond rear walls An extension on a side wall"

findings.problem: The drawing label 3m is run into the body text between two paragraphs.
findings.evidence: tree: "extensions from side walls. 3m  h) the enlarged part of the dwellinghouse"

findings.problem: The page sits under a heading "X" that is not in the document, so the Class A side and rear extension limits are not under Class A.
findings.evidence: source: "Rear and side extensions ... The extension must: (i) extend no more than 6 metres beyond the rear wall" / tree heading_path: "X > Text"

findings.problem: The tree has a number 33 before the drawing label 6m that is not printed on the page.
findings.evidence: source: "For example:" then drawing label "6m" / tree: "For example: 33 6m  23 In the following example"

findings.problem: The bold sub-heading is read as running body text.
findings.evidence: tree: "it would not be permitted development. Rear and side extensions Where an extension fills the area"

findings.problem: The cross mark beside the drawings is read as a chapter heading "X", and the Class A text around it is put under that heading.
findings.evidence: source: boxed cross "X" beside each drawing / tree: chapter title "X", heading_path "X > Text"

findings.problem: Drawing labels and the page number are run into the body text.
findings.evidence: tree: "An application for planning permission would therefore be required. 3m 3m" and "26 In some situations"

findings.problem: The cross mark beside the drawing is read as a chapter heading "X", and the Class A text around it is put under that heading.
findings.evidence: source: boxed cross "X" beside the drawing / tree: chapter title "X", heading_path "X > Text"

findings.problem: Drawing labels and page numbers are run into the body text.
findings.evidence: source: "For example:" ... "In the example above" / tree: "26 In some situations", "For example: 3m B", "A In the example above"

findings.problem: The page's sections, including limit (ja), sit under a heading "X" that is not a heading in the document (it looks like the cross mark of a diagram), so the rule is not under its Class A parent.
findings.evidence: tree: "X > (ja) any total enlargement (being the enlarged part together with any existing"

findings.problem: Limit (ja) is split in two: its first printed line is read as a heading and the rest of the same sentence as body text.
findings.evidence: source: "(ja) any total enlargement (being the enlarged part together with any existing enlargement of the original dwellinghouse" / tree: title "(ja) any total enlargement (being the enlarged part together with any existing"

findings.problem: The labels of the diagram are read as a table with an invented column name, though the page has no table.
findings.evidence: tree: columns "Drawing label", row "Enlarged part of house (A) that extends beyond side wall of house remains less than half the width of the original house"

findings.problem: Loose diagram labels are run into the end of the body paragraph.
findings.evidence: source: "extension (as it does not join it)." / tree: "(as it does not join it). 3m  B A width of"

findings.problem: The figure's labels lose the words "width of" from the long label.
findings.evidence: source: "half the width of the original house" / tree: "half the", "the", "original", "house"

findings.problem: Page numbers are left inside the running text.
findings.evidence: tree: "planning permission. 27 The next example" and "pages 18, 21 and 27). 28 (k) it would consist"

findings.problem: The page number is left inside the running text, between two paragraphs.
findings.evidence: source: "should not be included in this measurement." / tree: "should not be included in this measurement. 35 This 0.2m set back"

findings.problem: The diagram is read as a table, with the label "Roof Slope" used as the column heading over the 0.15 metres limit, so the limit reads as a value for the roof slope instead of the protrusion.
findings.evidence: source: diagram labels "Roof Slope", "No more than 0.15 metres", "(This diagram is not to scale)" / tree: columns "Roof Slope", row "No more than 0.15 metres"

findings.problem: The page number is left inside the running text.
findings.evidence: tree: "as protruding from the original roof. 38 (c) it would result"

findings.problem: The heading "Class H – microwave antenna" is read as body text, so the Class H limits sit under the "Conditions" heading of an earlier class instead of under their own heading.
findings.evidence: source: heading "Class H – microwave antenna" / tree: heading_path "Other Classes under Part 1 > Conditions > Text", text "Class H – microwave antenna This provides permitted development rights"

findings.problem: The page number is left at the end of the running text.
findings.evidence: tree: "on a building which exceeds 15 metres in height 49"
